title: Temperance Meaning: Find a Balance That Lets Different Needs Work Together

hook: Water is still flowing between the cups. Temperance is about continual adjustment: combining time, energy and needs in a way you can sustain.

sections.title: The hands pour, while the feet stand in two places

An angel in a white robe spreads red wings, its lowered gaze directed toward two gold cups. One cup is higher than the other, with blue water flowing diagonally between them. A circle with a central dot appears on its forehead, surrounded by rays. On the chest, an upward-pointing triangle sits inside a square, with lettering visible above.

One foot is in the water and the other on the bank; the feet are apart. Yellow flowers and long green leaves grow on the right. To the left, a path crosses rolling green ground toward blue mountains and a yellow glow behind them. The figure is steady, but neither the cups nor the feet are symmetrically placed. Their positions need to work together to hold the posture. [View the card](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:RWS_Tarot_14_Temperance.jpg)

The distant crown is not clear in this scan, so we attribute it to Waite’s account rather than claiming it is plainly visible. sections.title: Upright: Adjust toward something sustainable
sections.bodyMarkdown:
We use Temperance to explore proportion and cooperation. You need not do the maximum every time. Notice what changes when you add or reduce a little, then find a balance that suits current conditions. Study and rest, speaking and listening, planning and flexibility may all require such ongoing adjustment.

Two needs existing together does not make an equal split automatically fair. Sometimes the urgent need must come first, followed by time for the other to recover. Keep looking at the whole situation instead of treating one number as permanently correct.

sections.title: Reversed: Find the specific mismatch
sections.bodyMarkdown:
The reversed card can suggest uneven effort, incompatible ways of working or a rhythm disrupted by too many changes. Where do the parts fail to connect? Do schedules clash, handovers miss something, or do you alternate between all-out effort and a complete stop?

Waite’s upright list includes moderation and management. His reversed list includes disunion and competing interests, as well as historical associations with religious institutions. We use the practical connections as reading prompts, without reducing the card to a health diagnosis. Temperance cannot decide medication doses, dietary restrictions or treatment plans. [Waite, Part III, §3, entry 14](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pkt0303.htm)

sections.title: Make “the right amount” something you can try
sections.bodyMarkdown:
If exam preparation means ten hours in one weekend day and nothing during the week, try shorter, regular sessions for a week. Record what you finish and what you remember the next day, then adjust the length. Consistency need not mean doing exactly the same amount every day.

Two people write a report: one values speed, the other detail. Agree that the first draft will settle the structure and the next round will check the facts. Their strengths can then contribute at different stages instead of constantly interrupting each other.

When family care and work both intensify, separate what you must do personally, what can be negotiated and what can wait. If someone expects you to make every adjustment without making any themselves, the reversed card can also prompt a new discussion of the workload rather than more silent accommodation.

articleMarkdown:
# Temperance Meaning: Find a Balance That Lets Different Needs Work Together

Card: Temperance  
Number: XIV · RWS Major Arcana  
Keywords: Harmony, Proportion, Integration

**Upright quick take:** Ease off the all-out effort. Adjust the balance and pace so things can work more smoothly.  
**Reversed quick take:** The mix is off and the rhythm is uneven. Find what is getting too much and what is not getting enough.

Water is still flowing between the cups. Temperance is about continual adjustment: combining time, energy and needs in a way you can sustain.

## The hands pour, while the feet stand in two places

An angel in a white robe spreads red wings, its lowered gaze directed toward two gold cups. One cup is higher than the other, with blue water flowing diagonally between them. A circle with a central dot appears on its forehead, surrounded by rays. On the chest, an upward-pointing triangle sits inside a square, with lettering visible above.

One foot is in the water and the other on the bank; the feet are apart. Yellow flowers and long green leaves grow on the right. To the left, a path crosses rolling green ground toward blue mountains and a yellow glow behind them. The figure is steady, but neither the cups nor the feet are symmetrically placed. Their positions need to work together to hold the posture. [View the card](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:RWS_Tarot_14_Temperance.jpg)

## Harmony takes active adjustment

Waite describes the liquid as the essences of life passing between the cups. He says that although he uses a masculine pronoun, the angel is neither male nor female. He places the feet on land and water, and the distant light and crown, within religious symbolism of life, then discusses harmony between psychic and material natures. The distant crown is not clear in this scan, so we attribute it to Waite’s account rather than claiming it is plainly visible. [Waite, Part II, XIV](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pktar14.htm)

## Upright: Adjust toward something sustainable

We use Temperance to explore proportion and cooperation. You need not do the maximum every time. Notice what changes when you add or reduce a little, then find a balance that suits current conditions. Study and rest, speaking and listening, planning and flexibility may all require such ongoing adjustment.

Two needs existing together does not make an equal split automatically fair. Sometimes the urgent need must come first, followed by time for the other to recover. Keep looking at the whole situation instead of treating one number as permanently correct.

## Reversed: Find the specific mismatch

The reversed card can suggest uneven effort, incompatible ways of working or a rhythm disrupted by too many changes. Where do the parts fail to connect? Do schedules clash, handovers miss something, or do you alternate between all-out effort and a complete stop?

Waite’s upright list includes moderation and management. His reversed list includes disunion and competing interests, as well as historical associations with religious institutions. We use the practical connections as reading prompts, without reducing the card to a health diagnosis. Temperance cannot decide medication doses, dietary restrictions or treatment plans. [Waite, Part III, §3, entry 14](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pkt0303.htm)

## Make “the right amount” something you can try

If exam preparation means ten hours in one weekend day and nothing during the week, try shorter, regular sessions for a week. Record what you finish and what you remember the next day, then adjust the length. Consistency need not mean doing exactly the same amount every day.

Two people write a report: one values speed, the other detail. Agree that the first draft will settle the structure and the next round will check the facts. Their strengths can then contribute at different stages instead of constantly interrupting each other.

When family care and work both intensify, separate what you must do personally, what can be negotiated and what can wait. If someone expects you to make every adjustment without making any themselves, the reversed card can also prompt a new discussion of the workload rather than more silent accommodation.

## Practice: Try a small adjustment

Choose two needs that keep clashing, such as uninterrupted work and timely replies. Describe the current arrangement, then try one small change: fixed reply windows during the day, with alerts silenced at other times. After a week, check whether both work and communication have improved before keeping or changing it.

## A common misreading

Temperance does not mean always doing less, suppressing desire or compromising in every conflict. It concerns a workable combination. If a demand crosses a line of safety or respect, a clear refusal can also help make life sustainable again.

## Read next

Strength: compare steadying a strong reaction with regulating your pace over time; The Star: observe other ways of depicting flowing water, renewal and hope.

sourceRecord.title: 节制牌义 把分寸调好，让不同需要一起运作
sourceRecord.hook: 两只杯子之间，水还在流。节制关心的是持续调整：怎样搭配时间、精力与需求，才能做得长久。
sourceRecord.uprightQuickTake: 别一口气用太猛，调好比例和节奏，事情会更顺。
sourceRecord.reversedQuickTake: 搭配失衡、节奏乱了，先找出哪一头太多、哪一头不够。

sections.title: 手上在调水，脚下跨着两处
paragraphs: 白袍天使展开红色双翼，低垂的目光朝向手中的两只金杯。杯子一高一低，蓝色水流斜着连接它们。额头有圆中一点的符号，周围放射光线；胸前方框里套着向上的三角形，上方还能看见字形。
一只脚踏在水里，另一只立于岸边，两脚没有并拢。右侧长着黄色花朵和细长绿叶；左侧一条小路穿过绿色起伏，通向蓝色山峰，山后发出黄色光芒。整个人物很稳，杯与脚的安排却都不完全对称：需要一直配合，才能维持这个姿态。[查看本篇牌面](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:RWS_Tarot_14_Temperance.jpg)

sections.title: 调和是主动的过程
paragraphs: Waite 把杯间流动称为生命本质的倾注，并说明自己虽使用男性代词，天使形象却不属男性或女性。他将水陆两脚、远处的光与冠放在宗教性的生命象征中，最后谈到精神与物质性质的调和。远处的冠在扫描里并不清晰，因此这里把它作为 Waite 的解释，不冒充人人一眼可见的细节。[Waite 第二部 XIV](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pktar14.htm)

sections.title: 正位 一点点调到能持续的状态
paragraphs: 本站用节制讨论分寸与配合。你不必每次做到最多，可以观察多一点、少一点会怎样，再找到适合目前条件的比例。学习与休息、表达与倾听、计划与弹性，都可能需要这样的往返调整。
两种需要并存，并不意味着各分一半就是公平。有些时候必须先处理更紧急的一边，再安排另一边恢复；重要的是持续看见整体，而不是把单一数字当作永远正确的标准。

sections.title: 逆位 找出不协调的具体位置
paragraphs: 逆位可提示投入失衡、合作方式不合，或变化太多导致节奏散掉。先问是哪两个部分接不上：时间表互相冲突，任务交接遗漏，还是总在猛冲与完全停摆之间摇晃？
Waite 的正位词表提到适度与管理，逆位包含不合与利益竞争，同时也列了宗教机构等旧式联想；本篇采用前者作为阅读线索，没有把整张牌缩成健康诊断。节制不能替你决定药物剂量、饮食限制或治疗方案。[Waite 第三部 §3，第14条](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pkt0303.htm)

sections.title: 把「适量」说得可以操作
paragraphs: 准备考试时，周末一口气学十小时，平日又完全不碰。可先试一周较短的固定练习，记录能完成多少、第二天是否记得，再调整时长；稳定不必等于每天做得一样多。
两个人共同写报告，一个重视速度，一个在意细节。可先约定初稿只解决结构，下一轮再核查事实，让两种优势在不同阶段接上，减少互相打断。
照顾家庭与处理工作同时变忙时，把必须亲自做、可协商、能暂缓的事分开。若别人只要求你不断配合却不承担任何调整，逆位也可提醒你重新谈分工，而不是继续吞下所有不便。

sections.title: 练习 做一次小幅调整
paragraphs: 选一组总在冲突的需要，例如「安静做事」与「及时回复」。写下现状，再试一个小变化：一天固定几个回复窗口，其他时段关掉提示。一周后看工作和沟通是否都改善，再决定保留或修改。

sections.title: 容易看错的地方
paragraphs: 节制不等于永远少做、压住欲望，也不要求每场冲突都折中。它关心合适的搭配；当某项要求已经越过安全或尊重的底线，明确拒绝也能帮助生活恢复可持续的状态。
